scenarioPaths.narrative: Publisher submits complete artifact and evidence, review marks it installable, and payout stays a separate handoff.
scenarioPaths.safeOutcome: listing can show accepted review evidence while payout and support execution remain external handoffs

scenarioPaths.narrative: Missing SBOM or vulnerability evidence blocks installability and keeps publisher copy in remediation state.
scenarioPaths.safeOutcome: publisher receives customer-safe remediation guidance instead of approval or storefront visibility

scenarioPaths.narrative: Stale provenance or unknown catalog approval yields rejected or yanked copy and no launch claim.
scenarioPaths.safeOutcome: portal surfaces owner route, limitation, and migration guidance without proofless claims

scenarioPaths.narrative: Yanked or payout-blocked states route to support and commercial owners with approved limitation wording.
scenarioPaths.safeOutcome: support can explain the state without customer data, support tooling, or payout execution

accessibilityNotes: Keyboard order follows submission, evidence, review outcome, remediation, yank guidance, payout handoff, and support route.
Screen reader labels include publisher role, listing state, evidence state, review outcome, proof mode, and owner route.
Contrast is not the only state signal; blocked, rejected, yanked, unsupported, and scope-out states use explicit text.
Motion is optional; upload, review, and yank transitions must respect reduced-motion preferences.
scopeOut: No artifact hosting, Registry storage, package hosting, or signing runtime.
No payout provider, tax collection, bank account, settlement, or money movement implementation.
No security scanner, conformance runner, approval service, or policy engine implementation.
No production publisher portal UI, storefront, support queue, or support automation.
No customer-data access or launch claim without evidence.
